newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends mixed, nearbys gain on snow.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends mixed, nearbys gain on snow.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended mixed, with nearbys gaining on commercial buying tied to continuing transportation problems caused by winter weather in the northern U.S. Plains, traders said.
Another blizzard hit the area Wednesday, making roads impassable and tying up grain movement, traders said.
"They had interstates closed in North Dakota and Minnesota again. That's causing more problems. We're taking all our stocks out and we're not rebuilding them," one trader said.
MGE spring wheat settled 1-1/2 cents per bushel lower to 3-1/2 cents higher, with March up 3-1/2 cents at $3.89-1/2.

Commercial buying came from Continental, which bought 1.2 million March bushels, and from Cargill, which bought 700,000 March. General Mills and Bay State, which both have large milling interests, each bull-spread at least 400,000 March/May.
Traders said the March/May spread was bid at 15-1/2 cents, premium March, at the open but traded as wide as 17 cents.
The MGE estimated Wednesday's spring wheat futures volume at 13.9 million bushels, down from 17.6 million Tuesday.
MGE barley futures closed unchanged to one cent per cwt lower, with March down one cent at $6.69.
